title: docs(changeset): correct two pending changesets whose present-tense claims a later PR falsified
body:
Fixes #8617

`Clause-②: no`

Two unreleased changesets each carried a present-tense claim that a **later, separate PR has since falsified**. A changeset body publishes **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG, so both sentences would have shipped as published false statements. This PR corrects exactly those sentences and nothing else.

## 1. The window — re-measured by this seat, ⛔ no reading carried from the card

Triage's own correction (comment 5619376700) closes with 取卡时请自己重跑那条 `git ls-tree`,⛔ 不要沿用本卡任何一次的读数. So it was re-run on a freshly fetched `origin/main`:

```
$ git fetch origin main && git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- .changeset/
```

| | |
|---|---|
| measured at | **2026-09-10T15:56:06Z** (re-confirmed unchanged at push time, 16:03Z) |
| `origin/main` tip | `4d65991c5766b77bbc95b7b1ea93fb7154a8c7c7`, commit date **2026-09-10T15:31:10+00:00** |
| **control** — total entries under `.changeset/` | **1338** (1337 `*.md` + `config.json`); triage measured 1327 on 2026-09-10T13:11Z |
| `.changeset/6794-notify-submitter-default.md` | **present — still pending** |
| `.changeset/core-datascope-field-and-comparison-guards-7751.md` | **present — still pending** |

The control moved 1327 → 1338 across those ~2h45m, so the directory is genuinely being read and the two hits are readings, not a stuck listing. **The window is open**: neither changeset has been consumed by a release, so both sentences are still correctable.

Neither file had been touched since it was written — `git log` on the two paths returns their original landing commits (`21993e4a9` #6831 and `5aed9e4eb` #8048) and nothing since.

## 2. Instance one — `.changeset/6794-notify-submitter-default.md`

**Before** (lines 30-33, verbatim):

> Deliberately scoped to `notifySubmitter`. The sibling controller
> `escalation.enabled` is a separate, on-hold card (objectui#6620) whose default
> flips on a *future* spec bump; installed spec and table agree on it today, and
> generalising this assertion across the block would arm that card's tripwire here.

**After:**

> Deliberately scoped to `notifySubmitter`. The sibling controller
> `escalation.enabled` is a separate card (objectui#6620) whose default flipped on
> a spec bump that has since landed — installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 returns
> `enabled: true`, and PR objectui#8615 has matched the table's declaration to it,
> so installed spec and table agree on it today. When this was written that bump
> was still ahead, and generalising this assertion across the block would have
> armed that card's tripwire here.

### The measurements that prove it was false

**a. The spec bump is past, not future.** Run against the installed package, through the `@objectstack/spec/automation` subpath the card names:

```
installed @objectstack/spec version: 17.4.0
safeParse success: true
parsed data: {"enabled":true,"timeoutHours":24,"action":"notify","notifySubmitter":true}
```

`ApprovalEscalationSchema.safeParse({ timeoutHours: 24 })` yields `enabled: true` on the version this tree actually installs (17.4.0 — the card was filed against 17.3.0; it has bumped again since). ⇒ "flips on a *future* spec bump" is false.

**b. The table has already been flipped to match.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts` now declares `defaultValue: 'true'` for `escalation.enabled`, and the commit that changed it is in `main`:

```
b1a14f28e082c96f36d7a2b9c9202f210814fcc6  2026-09-08T16:52:56+00:00
  fix(app-shell): declare the spec's `escalation.enabled` default in the flow-node inspector (#8615)

-  { id: 'escalation.enabled', ... defaultValue: 'false', ... }
+  { id: 'escalation.enabled', ... defaultValue: 'true',  ... }
```

**c. `objectui#6620` is not on hold.** It is **closed as completed**, 2026-09-08T17:09:45Z, closed by PR #8615. ⇒ "on-hold card" is false, and it is false by the same event.

**d. The tripwire clause.** With spec `true` and table `'true'`, generalising the reconciliation assertion across the block would now simply pass — it would arm nothing. Present tense "would arm" is false today; changed to "would have armed", which is what was true when the sentence was written.

### ⭐ What was NOT edited, because it measures TRUE

> installed spec and table agree on it today

This is the clause the card lists as false, and it **is not**. Measured: spec returns `enabled: true` (a), table declares `'true'` (b) — **they agree**. What actually happened is that the pair went false when the spec bumped and true again when #8615 flipped the table, so the card's account of it (written before #8615 was read into the picture) does not hold. Per the fence — a sentence that is still true is reported, not edited — the clause is **kept verbatim**; only the surrounding false tense is repaired around it.

## 3. Instance two — `.changeset/core-datascope-field-and-comparison-guards-7751.md`

**Before** (line 11, verbatim):

> That third case is deliberately stricter than `evaluateCondition` in `@object-ui/permissions`, which this card was filed to converge with. Reading with `hasOwnProperty` alone — the sibling's shape — collapses "inherited" into "absent", and absent ADMITS on a negative operator, so the sibling still returns `true` for `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }` on every record (filed as objectui#8044).

**After:**

> That third case was deliberately stricter than `evaluateCondition` in `@object-ui/permissions` as that evaluator then stood, which this card was filed to converge with. Reading with `hasOwnProperty` alone — the sibling's shape at the time — collapses "inherited" into "absent", and absent ADMITS on a negative operator, so the sibling returned `true` for `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }` on every record (filed as objectui#8044, and fixed since by PR objectui#8669, which ported this three-case read into the sibling).

### The measurements that prove it was false

**a. PR #8669 is in `main`.**

```
2609812d2  fix(permissions): read a condition's field in three cases, not two (#8669)
```

**b. The sibling no longer reads with `hasOwnProperty` alone.** `packages/permissions/src/evaluator.ts` now carries the identical three-case read, and its own header records it as "a port of the shape objectui#7751 landed in `readField` in `packages/core/src/data-scope/DataScopeManager.ts`":

```ts
// packages/permissions/src/evaluator.ts — readField, as it stands after #8669
  if (PROTOTYPE_FIELD_NAMES.has(field)) return { readable: false };
  if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(record, field)) return { readable: true, value: record[field] };
  if (field in Object(record)) return { readable: false };
  return { readable: true, value: undefined };
```

`evaluateCondition` turns `readable: false` into `return false`. ⇒ `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }` **denies** today; "still returns `true`" is false. That also falsifies the two clauses in front of it in the same sentence — core's third case is no longer *stricter* than the sibling, and `hasOwnProperty` alone is no longer *the sibling's shape*. All three were falsified by the one PR, so all three are put in the past tense together.

**c. Runtime confirmation**, not only a source read — the pin that PR #8669 shipped:

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run packages/permissions/src/__tests__/evaluator.prototype-guard-8044.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)                       exit 0
```

It asserts `admits('toString', 'neq', 'x', record) === false` for every unlisted prototype member.

### What was NOT edited in this file, because it measures TRUE

- *"The sibling requires `typeof === 'number'` on both sides"* — true: `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` in `evaluator.ts` still test `typeof value === 'number' && typeof condition.value === 'number'`.
- *"the sibling already refused it"* (a non-string `contains` value) — true: `typeof condition.value === 'string'`.
- *"`ne` / `nin` here versus `neq` / `not_in` in the sibling, and the sibling's `is_null` / `is_not_null` which this evaluator does not implement, remain exactly as they were"* — true: `DataScopeManager` still spells `ne`/`nin` with no null arms; `evaluator.ts` still spells `neq`/`not_in`/`is_null`/`is_not_null`. PR #8669 changed the field read, not the spellings.

## 4. Scope

- ⛔ **Neither bump level touched** — the overwrite gate reads this back for both files: `declared at base: @object-ui/app-shell: patch` / `declares now: @object-ui/app-shell: patch`, and `@object-ui/core: minor` / `@object-ui/core: minor`.
- ⛔ Neither changeset deleted; both describe real shipped changes that owe a CHANGELOG entry.
- ⛔ No other changeset touched (2 files changed, +7 −4, prose only).
- ⛔ `content/docs/releases/**` untouched. ⛔ No release note written or re-framed.
- ⛔ The structural half of the card — that nothing re-reads a pending changeset when a later PR falsifies it — is **not** addressed here and no gate for it is built here; #8617 remains open on that half for the PM to file separately.

## 5. Checks — exit codes captured before any pipe

| command | exit | verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** | `✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` (2 files changed, 0 published source) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | **0** | `✅ All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | **0** | ✅ No changeset declares a major bump. |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` | **0** | report-only; reports both files as modified-not-added with **bump levels unchanged** — case 2, "correcting a declaration on purpose" |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | **0** | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 7200 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | **0** | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `pnpm lint:root` | **0** | `✖ 32 problems (0 errors, 32 warnings)` — all pre-existing, none in this diff |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/permissions/src/__tests__/evaluator.prototype-guard-8044.test.ts` | **0** | `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 34 passed (34)` — evidence for §3, not a gate this diff owes |

Every `.changeset/**`-triggered workflow (`changeset-guard.yml`, `changeset-presence.yml`) runs exactly the scripts above; all four ran locally green. ⛔ Nothing was skipped, disabled or quarantined.

⚠️ **A green gate is not the acceptance evidence here** — nothing in this repository parses changeset prose for truth, so every gate stays green whether or not this is fixed. The evidence is §1-§3: the corrected text read back, plus the tree measurements showing what each sentence asserted was false.

## 6. Fork not resolved

`.changeset/6794-notify-submitter-default.md` line 9 reads *"the installed `@objectstack/spec` (17.2.0) defaults the key to `true`"*. Installed is now **17.4.0**, so the parenthetical is stale — but the claim it carries (`notifySubmitter` defaults to `true`) is **still true on 17.4.0**, and the version reads as the provenance pin of the original measurement rather than a claim about today. Left unedited on the narrower reading; flagged so the release editor can settle it.
